layout_sources: https://github.com/rsi2m/ofxstatement-ee-swedbank/blob/HEAD/src/ofxstatement/plugins/ee_swedbank.py (Estonian Swedbank CSV: semicolon, %d.%m.%Y, date col 2, payer/payee col 3, details col 4, unsigned amount col 5, D/K col 7, archive id col 8, type col 9 with AS/K2/LS rows skipped, first two rows skipped)

https://github.com/bank2ynab/bank2ynab/blob/develop/bank2ynab/data/bank2ynab.conf [LV Swedbank] (statement.csv, semicolon, 2 header rows, 4 footer rows, 12 columns, D/K indicator in column 7, %d.%m.%Y) and https://github.com/firefly-iii/import-configurations/blob/main/lv/swedbank/default.json

https://pypi.org/project/ofxstatement-lithuanian/ 1.2.0 tests/samples/swedbank.csv (the same Baltic Swedbank layout in Lithuanian: every field quoted, a trailing separator, row types 10 opening / 20 line / 82 turnover D and K / 86 closing, codes AS, K, MK, K2, LS, UTF-8, LF)
notes: Swedbank Estonia internet bank account statement CSV. Every field double-quoted, semicolon-separated, a trailing ; on each line, UTF-8, LF. Row type (Reatüüp) 10 is the opening balance (Algsaldo), 20 a line, 82 the debit and credit turnovers (Käive), 86 the closing balance (Lõppsaldo). Dates DD.MM.YYYY; Summa is unsigned with a comma decimal, the sign is in Deebet/Kreedit (D = money out, K = money in). The Estonian column names are from memory (the sources confirm positions and codes; the Lithuanian sample has 16 columns). Oldest first. Opening and closing come from the 10 and 86 rows.
